summary_zh.motivation: 研究非等原子比FeNiCoAl高熵合金的LPBF打印性及力学性能。
summary_zh.method: 采用激光粉末床熔融制备合金，分析打印参数对组织和性能的影响。
summary_zh.result: 成功打印出无缺陷样品，获得了优异的力学性能。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微组织观察和力学测试验证打印质量和性能。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the printability, microstructure, and mechanical properties of a non-equiatomic FeNiCoAl-based high-entropy alloy fabricated by laser powder bed fusion.
summary_en.method: Laser powder bed fusion was used to fabricate the alloy, and the effects of processing parameters on microstructure and mechanical properties were analyzed.
summary_en.result: Defect-free samples with excellent mechanical properties were obtained.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural characterization and mechanical testing were performed to validate print quality and performance.

papers.title: The Knee-Fix study: study protocol for a randomised controlled trial evaluating cemented and cementless components in total knee arthroplasty.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is an effective procedure for patients with a variety of knee conditions. The main cause of aseptic TKA failure is implant loosening, which has been linked to poor cement mantle quality. Cementless components were introduced to offer better longer-term biological fixation through osseointegration; however, early designs led to increased rate of revision due to a lack of initial press-fit and bony ingrowth. Newer highly porous metal designs may alleviate this issue but randomised data of fully uncemented TKA (tibial, femoral, patella) is lacking. The aim of the Knee-Fix study is to investigate the long-term implant survival and patient outcomes of fully uncemented compared with cemented fixation in TKA. Our study hypothesis was that uncemented TKA would be as clinically reliable and durable as the gold-standard cemented TKA. METHODS: The Knee-Fix study is a two-arm, single-blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial with 160 patients in each arm and follow-up at 6 weeks, 6 months, 12 months, 24 months, 5 years and 10 years. The primary outcome of interest is implant fixation, which will be measured by assessment of postoperative progressive radiolucencies with the Knee Society Total Knee Arthroplasty Roentgenographic Evaluation and Scoring System. Secondary outcome measures are patient-reported outcomes, measured using Oxford Knee Score (OKS), International Knee Society System (IKSS), Forgotten Joint Score-12 (FJS-12), EuroQol (EQ-5D-5L), VAS Pain, Patient Satisfaction Score and Net Promoter Score. DISCUSSION: While cemented fixation remains the gold standard, a growing proportion of TKA are now implanted cementless. Highly porous metal cementless components for TKA can offer several benefits including potentially improved biological fixation; however, long-term outcomes need further investigation. This prospective study will help discern long-term differences between the two techniques. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ACTRN12616001624471 . Registered trial name: Knee-Fix study (Cemented vs Uncemented Total Knee Replacement). Registered on 24 November 2016.

summary_en.motivation: To compare long-term implant survival and patient outcomes of fully uncemented versus cemented fixation in total knee arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Two-arm, single-blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial with 160 patients per arm and follow-up up to 10 years.
summary_en.result: Primary outcome is implant fixation measured by progressive radiolucencies; secondary outcomes include patient-reported scores.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; it is a clinical trial protocol.
